heading: EXT. FISHING TRAWLER "MARGARET ANN" - DECK - NIGHT

units.text: EXT. FISHING TRAWLER "MARGARET ANN" - DECK - NIGHT
A rusted forty-foot trawler wallows in black swell off the breakwater, nets heaped in wet coils, a single work lamp swinging on its cable.
Diesel and salt in the air.
SKIPPER BRODIE FENN, 50s, weathered, a gold tooth he shows when he lies, leans against the winch.
Beside him stands a STRANGER in a clean dry anorak, far too neat for a boat, holding a tablet in a waterproof sleeve.
You're the captain? I was told the catch would be on ice by midnight.
units.name: STRANGER

units.text: Catch is in the hold. Ice is a figure of speech.
units.name: BRODIE

units.text: The STRANGER taps the tablet.
ON TABLET: UNIT 4 - HARBOUR CUSTOMS - INSPECTION 06:00 - CLEAR
Customs clear at six. That gives us six hours to move forty crates of "cod" off this deck and into a van that does not officially exist.
units.name: STRANGER

units.text: And who might you be, friend, to know about vans?
units.name: BRODIE

units.text: The STRANGER glances up, finally, and unzips the anorak.
Underneath: a badge, a vest, a holstered sidearm.
Detective Marcus Hale, Maritime Task Force. And I'd stop smiling.
units.name: MARCUS

units.text: Cap'n! Cap'n, there's lights on the water!
units.name: THE CREW

units.text: Searchlights sweep across the swell, white and enormous.
A bullhorn crackles.
All units, this is Hale. Boarding in ninety seconds. Nobody leaves this deck.
units.name: MARCUS

units.text: You were on my boat for three weeks. You gutted my fish.
units.name: BRODIE

units.text: You make a lovely chowder, Skipper.
units.name: MARCUS

units.text: The work lamp SWINGS and shatters against the winch.
Darkness, then the harsh white of the searchlights on every face.
